invariants.name: agent_unique
invariants.statement: exactly one cell shows colour 6 at all times

invariants.name: nothing_rests_on_a_free_cell
invariants.statement: no movable has a free cell below it, and the agent has no cell below it that it could be deposited on — every state a reader can observe is a settle fixpoint, so there is nowhere left to fall

invariants.name: block_count
invariants.statement: exactly 1 cell(s) show colour 2 at all times

invariants.name: blocks_disjoint
invariants.statement: no two blocks ever occupy the same cell

claims.claimed: conditional — reversible on open floor, not across a one-way edge
claims.reversible: conditional — reversible on open floor, not across a one-way edge

claims.claimed: conditional — only where the agent can reach the far side of the block
claims.reversible: conditional — only where the agent can reach the far side of the block

rules.name: walk
rules.reversible: conditional — reversible on open floor, not across a one-way edge
rules.then: the agent moves one cell in direction D
rules.when: act=D and the target cell is inside the grid, is not a wall, and no mechanism claims it

rules.name: blocked_by_wall
rules.when: act=D and the target cell is outside the grid or is a wall

rules.name: fall
rules.then: that thing descends one cell, and this repeats to a fixpoint — a post-step settlement, appended to whatever rule ended the step, never tagged as a rule of its own
rules.when: a movable has a free cell directly below it, or the agent has a cell directly below it that the agent may be deposited on
rules.why: descending a ledge cannot be undone from below, so a fall is a one-way edge in the reachable graph and any rule witnessed only above a ledge gets exactly one witness

rules.name: agent_does_not_fall_onto_live_entities
rules.then: the agent does not descend into it — it stays where it is, hovering, until it walks in and triggers the effect properly
rules.when: the cell below the agent holds an uncollected token or an intact fragile tile
rules.why: an agent dropped onto a fragile tile would skip `interact` and leave the tile ARMED while rendering exactly as INTACT, and a state the frame cannot distinguish is a world that cannot be learned from its trace.  The hovering *is* visible — the token or tile is right there under the agent — so this is a rule a reader can witness rather than an unexplained exception

rules.name: up_is_inert
rules.then: the agent rises into it, then falls straight back during the same step's settlement, so the state after the step equals the state before it
rules.when: act=UP and the cell above the agent is plain floor
rules.why: scoped to plain floor because it is false otherwise, and was published unscoped: gravity claims no target cell, so UP into a fragile tile, a latch, a toggle or a shut cycler dispatches to that mechanism's `interact`, which fires *before* the fall back. One UP into a fragile tile returns the agent to where it started and leaves the tile permanently collapsed

rules.name: push
rules.reversible: conditional — only where the agent can reach the far side of the block
rules.then: the block moves one cell in direction D and the agent takes the block's old cell
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds a block and the cell beyond it in direction D is free

rules.name: blocked_by_block
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds a block and the cell beyond it is not free

spec.notes: Ledges and a shaft. `UP` is inert here — the agent moves and gravity settles it straight back — and descending a ledge cannot be undone, so the reachable graph is genuinely layered rather than a big reversible blob.
